newsitem.title: USA: Pamela Anderson Lee said "no" to topless scene.
newsitem.headline: Pamela Anderson Lee said "no" to topless scene.

text.p: Actress Pamela Anderson Lee, the former "Baywatch" star who has been sued for backing out of a movie deal, told a court on Friday she objected to baring her breasts in the film.
"It seemed like it was there for a cheap thrill," Lee said of the proposed topless sunbathing scene in the movie "Hello, She Lied."

The actress, best known as a swimsuit-clad lifeguard in TV's "Baywatch" series and who has bared all for Playboy magazine, told the court that she objected mostly, however, to the proposed script, which called for simulated sex scenes.
"I wanted to lose the sexual content and make it a better script," she said under direct questioning from plaintiff's attorney Adam Miller.
"Nudity has never been an issue with me," she told the attorney.
Asked to explain, she answered, "I had a very bad experience on one movie once."

Lee was sued for $5 million by The Private Movie Co., which alleged she broke an agreement to star in the film and pulled out because she had a better offer to make the feature film "Barb Wire," which was subsequently a box-office flop.

The Canadian-born actress, who is married to rock drummer Tommy Lee of the band Motley Crue, claimed she changed her mind about making "Hello, She Lied" after seeing the script. She objected because it entailed performing simulated sex, including nude scenes in a shower and on a pool table.
In testimony on Friday morning, Lee appeared to contradict herself. At one point she said emphatically: "I never dropped out of the film."
But later she said: "I dropped out of the film because I hated it and it had all the sexual content in it that I had been told would be removed."
The actress said she hired a writer of her own to rewrite some of the scenes for the film, which she envisaged as a "Steve Martin-type comedy."
"Everybody knew the script was not a very good script and we could do better," said Lee, who wore a short-sleeved black blouse that revealed a barbed-wire tattoo on her upper left arm.
But she said when she objected to one scene in which she was meant to simulate making love to a man in a gymnasium, the movie-makers changed only the location -- to a bedroom.

Several times in the morning session she rolled her eyes at Miller's questions about minutiae of the contract. The filmmakers contend they had a binding agreement with the actress, but Lee says they did not.
"Hello, She Lied" was later made as "Miami Hustler," with model Kathy Ireland in the lead role, and aired on the Showtime cable TV channel.
